questions.stem: 提示：有人喜歡和隊友一起打球，享受合作與競爭；也有人偏好獨自運動，自己決定時間與節奏。請仔細觀察下面兩張圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一團隊運動與圖二獨自運動兩種運動方式的不同；第二段評估這兩種運動方式對身心各有什麼好處與限制，並針對「高中生如何養成長期運動的習慣」提出一個具體做法。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有三個要求：第一段比較團隊運動與獨自運動；第二段評估兩種方式對身心的好處與限制，再針對「高中生如何養成長期運動的習慣」提出具體做法。比較點可以從圖中找：和隊友一起或一個人、放學後的球場或清晨的河堤與晚上的客廳、擊掌的熱鬧或戴耳機的安靜。第二段的做法要回應「長期」：只寫「多運動」或「找朋友打球」太空泛，要說明怎麼讓習慣持續下去。
evidence: 比較圖一團隊運動與圖二獨自運動兩種運動方式的不同

1.strategy_zh: 可以用自己運動半途而廢的經驗點出獨自運動的弱點（缺乏動力），再提出結合兩者優點的做法（例如找運動夥伴、互相記錄），讓做法直接回應評估。

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show two different ways to exercise. In Picture 1, six students are playing basketball on a school court. One player is jumping to pass the ball, and two teammates under the basket are giving each other a high five. In Picture 2, a young man is exercising alone. In the morning, he jogs along a river with earphones on, and in the evening, he stretches on a yoga mat, following a video on his laptop. The first picture is full of teamwork and excitement, while the second is calm and quiet.
Both kinds of exercise are good for the body and the mind, but each has its limits. Team sports teach us to work with others, and playing with friends is a great way to relieve stress. However, it is not easy to find enough players at the same time. Exercising alone is more flexible because we can choose when and where to do it. On the other hand, it is easy to give up when nobody is watching. Last semester, I started jogging by myself, but I stopped after only two weeks. To build a long-term habit, I suggest that students find an exercise partner and set a weekly goal together. For example, two friends can jog three times a week and check each other's progress online. In this way, they can keep their own schedule and still enjoy a partner's support.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
Although both pictures show people staying active, they capture two very different experiences of exercise. In Picture 1, six students in red and blue jerseys are playing a half-court basketball game at sunset; one player leaps to pass the ball, while two teammates under the hoop exchange a high five. Their water bottles and schoolbags lie on a bench nearby, as if they had rushed straight from class. Picture 2, on the other hand, follows a single young man through his day. At six in the morning, he jogs alone along a riverside path with earphones in, his sports watch showing 5.2 kilometers, and in the evening he stretches on a yoga mat in his living room, following a video on his laptop. In short, team sports depend on other people and a shared schedule, whereas solo workouts depend only on the individual's own timetable and self-discipline.
Each form of exercise benefits the body and mind in its own way, and each has its limits. Team sports build speed, cooperation, and a sense of belonging; after a close game, the stress of a long school day often seems to disappear. Yet they are hard to organize, since a game requires enough players, a court, and a time that suits everyone. Solo workouts fit easily into a busy schedule, steady running strengthens the heart, and the quiet of an early run can clear the mind. Their weakness is motivation: with no teammates waiting, skipping a session costs nothing. I know this from experience. Last spring, I bought new running shoes and promised myself that I would run every morning, but by the third week I was pressing the snooze button instead. What finally kept me going was joining a weekend running group, whose members noticed whenever I was missing. This suggests that a lasting habit needs both the freedom of solo exercise and the commitment of a team. Therefore, I propose that schools set up an exercise buddy program, in which students pair up, choose any activity they like, and record their workouts on a shared online chart that their homeroom teacher can check. Even if one partner prefers jogging and the other prefers basketball, they can still remind and encourage each other. After all, whether we keep exercising depends less on which sport we choose than on whether someone expects us to show up.

steady.comment_zh: 三項要求都有回應：第一段比較圖一六名學生打籃球、傳球與擊掌，和圖二年輕男子早上戴耳機沿河慢跑、晚上跟著影片在瑜伽墊上伸展，並用 while 歸納熱鬧與安靜的差異；第二段分別說明團隊運動能學合作、紓壓但難湊人數，獨自運動彈性高但容易放棄，以自己慢跑兩週就停的經驗佐證，再提出找運動夥伴、訂每週目標、上網互相檢查進度的做法。缺點是圖中時間、地點等細節取用較少，對身心好處的分析偏籠統；exercise 重複偏多，句型以並列句為主。未見文法、用字或標點錯誤。

top.comment_zh: 第一段細節豐富（紅藍球衣、夕陽、半場、水壺與書包、清晨六點、5.2 公里、客廳伸展），並以 whereas 歸納「團隊運動靠他人與共同時間、獨自運動靠自律」的根本差異；第二段分別評估兩種方式對身心的好處（速度、合作、歸屬感、紓壓；心肺、彈性、沉澱）與限制（難湊人與場地；缺乏動機），以買新跑鞋卻按貪睡鍵、加入週末跑團才持續的經驗帶出「需要自由也需要承諾」，再提出配對互相提醒的運動夥伴計畫，結尾見解有力。句構多變（分詞構句、非限定關係子句、propose that＋原形、depends less on…than on…），用字精準（leaps、self-discipline、sense of belonging、snooze button）。未見錯誤；篇幅偏長，但不影響分數。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段以圖中細節（六人、擊掌、慢跑、瑜伽墊）描述並歸納對比；第二段兩種方式的好處與限制都寫到，並以只慢跑兩週的經驗帶到找運動夥伴、每週設目標的具體做法。對身體方面的好處著墨較少，exercise 重複，用字平實；未發現語言錯誤。

top.comment_zh: 第一段用夕陽、紅藍球衣、水壺書包、5.2 公里等細節對照，並以 whereas 句歸納差異；第二段身心好處與限制具體，以半途而廢的經驗帶到「運動夥伴計畫」的具體做法，結尾有見解。句型與用字精準，未發現語言錯誤。
